clue.text: Joker loving to snort line, very keen on a party?

parts.note: a joker is a playing card, and also a wag known as a card

indicators.note: to snort something is to draw it up inside, so one piece is taken into the middle of another

parts.note: a synonym: kind and affectionate
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A comedian with a fondness for cocaine who loves a good party.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags joker as just one kind of card, and the 'party' is political rather than festive; 'snort' hints at drugs but only means take in.
explanation.definitionFit: A card-carrying member holds a membership card, so the phrase describes a committed, dedicated supporter of a political party.

clue.text: Head of Chinese State Intelligence is yawning

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Chinese
to state is to aver, assert
nous is common sense or intelligence

explanation.surface: A Chinese spy chief caught yawning at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawning chasm is wide open and gaping, which is the sense of a vast cave-like space.

clue.text: Devoid of mercy, like an incomplete Bible?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read cryptically: a Bible missing the Book of Ruth

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the word in two: the Old Testament book named after Ruth, and 'less' meaning without it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is an old word for pity, so to be without ruth is to be pitiless and cruel.

clue.text: Not demanding retiring copper must take the lead

indicators.note: taking the lead means going in front, so the metal piece is placed before the other one

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a retiring person is shy, bashful

explanation.surface: A timid policeman has to step up and lead, though the job isn't hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushy job is easy and comfortable, one that makes few demands on the person doing it.

clue.text: Record-holder is behind, checking heart on run

indicators.note: to check is to hold back or restrain, so the outer word holds the others within it

parts.note: the rear is the behind, the back part
the heart of a matter is its gist
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An athlete holding a record is behind, checking their heart rate during a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-holder' reads as a champion athlete but means an official who keeps records; 'heart on run' keeps its two parts together as one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A registrar is an official who keeps registers of births, marriages and deaths, so a keeper of records.

clue.text: Turn up in Mongolian dwelling? One might be potted

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: a yurt is the round felt tent of Mongolian nomads

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is written from bottom to top, back to front

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go

explanation.surface: Someone appears, in a question, at a nomad's tent on the steppe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potted' suggests snooker or a house plant, but here it means sold in a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogurt is commonly sold in small pots, so it is a fair example of something potted.

clue.text: She's related new and extremely innovative chronicle

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters are kept from each of the following words

parts.note: the two end letters of innovative
the two end letters of chronicle

explanation.surface: A woman has told a new and very original story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She's related' reads as 'she has narrated', but means she is a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a female relative, the daughter of a brother or sister, so she is related.

clue.text: Some latitude over shot headed by right back

indicators.note: headed by means the following piece goes at the front of the others
going back means the abbreviation is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: RT is an abbreviation for right
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a pic is a photograph, a shot

explanation.surface: A football commentary: the right back heads the ball over after a shot.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are particular lines of latitude, so a tropic is some latitude.

clue.text: More fatuous, exclusive clothing article

indicators.note: clothing something wraps it, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: an exclusive group is an inner circle
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A rather silly item of exclusive designer wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly and empty, so the comparative inaner means more fatuous.

clue.text: Parisian bank ultimately cut interest completely

parts.note: rive is French for a riverbank, as in the Rive Gauche

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so the final letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of cut

explanation.surface: A Paris bank finally slashed its interest rate to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' looks financial in the surface; in the definition it is a verb meaning to hold someone's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To rivet someone is to grip their attention entirely, which is to interest them completely.

clue.text: French painter losing head about place for putting colour

indicators.note: about suggests turning round, so what is left is read backwards
losing its head means the painter's name drops its first letter

parts.note: Edgar Degas, French Impressionist painter
on a golf course the ball is putted on the green

explanation.surface: A French artist going mad over where to apply paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting' reads as placing paint, but it is the golf stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage green is a soft greyish-green shade named after the herb's leaves.

clue.text: Herb Alpert undressed, say, when playing

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of its outer layer, so the name loses its first and last letters
playing suggests the letters are moved about and performed in a new order

parts.note: Alpert without its outer letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: The trumpeter Herb Alpert performing naked, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like Herb Alpert's first name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsley is a common culinary herb with curly or flat green leaves.

clue.text: Press in numbers around important theatre figure

indicators.note: in places the verb inside the other piece
turned around means the abbreviation is read from back to front

parts.note: NOS is the abbreviation for numbers
to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: Journalists crowd round a star of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests the stage, but it is the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is the leading person in an operating theatre, so an important figure there.

clue.text: President's touring Scottish island, a bit of a sight

indicators.note: touring a place means going all round it, so the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: the president of a meeting is its chair, so 'chair's'
Ross is a name in the Scottish Highlands; the island tag is loose

explanation.surface: A head of state making a visit to a Hebridean island, rather a spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: The sight here is a gun sight, not a view. Ross is really a Scottish region rather than an island, so the clue stretches a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosshairs are the fine crossed lines in a telescopic gun sight, so they form part of one.

clue.text: Turkey portion, like one given to a child

parts.note: as means like
I is the Roman numeral one
a child is a minor in law

explanation.surface: A slice of the Christmas turkey, the sort you'd give a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' reads as the bird; it is the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia Minor is the historical name for Anatolia, the Asian part of modern Turkey.

clue.text: The Ancient Mariner, say, returns for Arabian big fish

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Coleridge's poem is The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, an example of a rime

explanation.surface: A sailor comes back from the sea with a huge catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big fish' is an idiom for an important person, not a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a ruler or prince in Arab countries, so an important person, a big fish.

clue.text: Spooner's N. American diving bird may glow in the dark

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of neighbouring words

parts.note: the loon is the North American name for a diver; it takes the other word's opening sound
may and might are both modal verbs of possibility; this one takes the bird's opening sound

explanation.surface: A water bird that might be luminous at night.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of the two words gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonlight is the soft light of the moon seen at night, a glow in the dark sky.

clue.text: Top tennis player, holding soft drink, steps on it

indicators.note: holding something keeps it inside, so the player surrounds the letter

parts.note: top players in a tournament are seeds
P is piano, soft in music
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A leading tennis player with a soft drink in hand treads on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps on it' is the idiom for hurrying, not treading on something.
explanation.definitionFit: To step on it is to put one's foot on the accelerator, so to go faster.

clue.text: Maybe enjoy the Sun's introduction to burning question

indicators.note: an introduction comes first, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of burning
to question is to ask

explanation.surface: A tabloid's opening piece on a burning issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Sun' looks like the British tabloid newspaper, but it is the star you lie out under.
explanation.definitionFit: To bask is to lie relaxing in warmth, typically sunshine, so enjoying the sun is an example.

clue.text: Promos for covers of rubbish Britpop band put first

indicators.note: put first means the band's name goes ahead of the other piece

parts.note: Blur were a leading 1990s Britpop band

indicators.note: the covers of something are its outsides, so its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the end letters of rubbish

explanation.surface: Album sleeves for a dreadful Britpop group's promotional releases.
explanation.definitionFit: Blurbs are short promotional texts on book covers, so they are promos.

clue.text: Note haircut with perfect means of increasing volume

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
a crop is a short haircut
to hone is to sharpen or perfect

explanation.surface: A memo about getting a perfect haircut, with a tip on adding volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' hints at hair volume after the haircut, but it is loudness.
explanation.definitionFit: A microphone feeds sound to an amplifier, making it louder, so it is a means to raise volume.

clue.text: Something Britain had from legislator in Ireland

indicators.note: in places the legislator inside the name of the country

parts.note: Éire is the Irish name for Ireland
an MP, Member of Parliament, makes laws

explanation.surface: Britain took something from a lawmaker in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface brushes against the history of British rule in Ireland, which was part of the thing defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain once ruled a vast overseas empire, so an empire is something it had.

clue.text: Beer tucked into by American adult, one smashed at parties

indicators.note: a drink tucked into by someone has that person inside it, so the letter goes within the drink

parts.note: a pint of beer
A is an abbreviation for American
A is the film certificate for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up American swigs beer and ends up drunk at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashed' looks like slang for drunk, but the definition means struck open.
explanation.definitionFit: A piñata is a decorated container of sweets that children break open with sticks at parties.

clue.text: Game turned round: possibly I initially underestimated Man U

indicators.note: turned round means the abbreviation for the game is read backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be put in some other order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the start, so the first letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of underestimated
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football fan admits they underrated Manchester United and the game swung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man U' looks like the nickname for Manchester United, but the final U is the definition alone. RU is rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: U is the chemical symbol for uranium, a radioactive element.

clue.text: More beautiful female ditched a clothes horse

indicators.note: ditched means thrown away, so the abbreviation for female is removed

parts.note: fairer means prettier
F is short for female

explanation.surface: A prettier woman dumped a vain fashion-obsessed partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes horse' reads as a vain dresser but here means the drying frame.
explanation.definitionFit: An airer is a folding frame for drying laundry, which is literally called a clothes horse in Britain.

clue.text: One may fix an Ascot sporting event, given 151 pence

parts.note: a tie is a match in a cup competition
151 in Roman numerals
P is short for pence

explanation.surface: Someone could rig a race at Ascot racecourse for a small bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot looks like the racecourse, but an ascot is a broad neck scarf or tie.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie clip holds a necktie in place against the shirt, so it can fasten an ascot.

clue.text: Maybe the opening of a Sylvia Plath letter dragged awkwardly

parts.note: a letter's opening salutation names its recipient, starting with this word; maybe flags it as one possible letter
Plath's husband was the poet Ted Hughes, the likely addressee
surface context: the salutation belongs to a letter written by the poet

explanation.surface: A poet's letter that got lugged about clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' flags that this is just one letter Plath might have written; the whole phrase 'To Ted' is the salutation.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry or lug something heavy, so toted means hauled with effort.

clue.text: Cockney's hair dressing publication is an attractive item

indicators.note: dressing something covers it all round, so the hair word wraps the publication

parts.note: barnet is Cockney rhyming slang for hair, from Barnet Fair
a mag is a magazine

explanation.surface: A Londoner's hairstyle magazine is a desirable thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London district; its fair rhymes with hair. 'Attractive' sounds like looks but means magnetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar magnet is a straight piece of magnetised metal that attracts iron.

clue.text: Company founder seen on the box for honey

definitions.text: Company founder seen on the box
definitions.meaning: first meaning: Alan ..., founder of Amstrad and host of the British TV show The Apprentice
second meaning: a term of endearment

explanation.walkthrough: 'The box' is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are affectionate pet names for a loved one, and the businessman's surname matches too.

clue.text: Sky viewer may see this tip-top snooker feat, pocketing balls

indicators.note: pocketing something takes it inside, so the phrase encloses the balls

parts.note: an excellent shot in snooker
snooker has fifteen red balls, the reds

explanation.surface: A TV snooker viewer watches a superb shot sink several balls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky' suggests the satellite TV channel, but it is the night sky seen through a telescope.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Red Spot is a giant storm on Jupiter, visible to an astronomer through a telescope.
